title: Learn UI/UX for Free - 30 Videos in 30 Days
why: Pure announcement trailer for the series (upload schedule, hashtag) - zero teaching content.

title: WHAT IS UI/UX? And which to focus on

best.what: clear UI-vs-UX definition via the ketchup-packet analogy plus real do/don't examples (password visibility icon, GDPR banners, click-to-enter walls)

why: Correct, jargon-free, no Figma - a kid can watch this and actually get the UI/UX distinction.

title: The Sweet Tools of UI/UX Design

best.what: "skills last forever, tools don't" - the one-line argument for why the specific design tool doesn't matter

why: Mostly a tour of Figma/Penpot/Protopie/Framer that our stack doesn't use; only the opening thesis is worth quoting to kids.

title: UI/UX Desktop Navigations in Figma (Challenge)

best.what: visual hierarchy explained through font-size choices for a nav vs a headline
the Stark contrast-checker plugin and the WCAG 4.5:1 ratio rule - concept transfers even without Figma

why: Real UI fundamentals (alignment, whitespace, contrast, hierarchy) explained well, but 30 minutes is 90% Figma clicking - needs a guide to pull the concepts out.

title: Who made the Best UI/UX Navigation? (Review)

best.what: rapid-fire worked examples of nav mistakes fixed live: contrast, spacing, icon placement, mixing italics/bold, CTA emphasis

why: A critique reel, not a tool tutorial - fast, concrete, good-vs-bad comparisons a teen can absorb by watching.

title: The UI/UX of Hero Sections (Challenge)

best.what: what every hero section needs (headline, subheadline, CTA, visual) and why the headline is always the largest element

why: Good structural concept for hero sections, but almost 25 minutes of Figma mechanics (plus a rambling keyboard-glitch tangent) to get it.

title: UI/UX Refactoring of your Hero Sections (Review)

best.what: one-by-one hero-section fixes: contrast, letter-spacing, CTA sizing, overlapping-text layering trick, line-height cleanup

why: Short, concrete, example-driven review - exactly the good-vs-bad format the brief flags as most useful for teens.

title: The UI/UX of Card Design (Challenge)

best.what: what a card is and why it groups a few pieces of data into one unit

why: Card-content hierarchy and spacing concepts are useful, but wrapped in a lot of icon-plugin and pen-tool Figma mechanics.

title: Who Designed the BEST UI/UX Cards?
why: No caption file - judged from title only. Same review format as XdtwJdFjoVs/cYnJLT36Oxo (both core), but unverified so marked more cautiously.

title: Learn Responsive Web Design (Challenge)

best.what: the core responsive mental model: collapse columns into rows at smaller widths, hamburger-menu pattern, reduce whitespace as screens shrink

why: Genuinely transferable web-design concept (how layouts should adapt), but delivered as 19 minutes of manual Figma resizing.

title: Who made the BEST Responsive Design?

best.what: the right way to collapse a 3-column card row into 2 columns without leaving an orphan card stranded in the middle

why: Fast, concrete good-vs-bad responsive-design examples across ~15 submissions - very watchable and on-topic.

title: Can you make THIS Design Responsive? (Challenge)
why: Just a challenge announcement (design a flight-ticket card responsively) - no teaching content, all in the companion review video.

title: Who Designed the BEST Responsive Card?

best.what: good vs. bad responsive restructuring: keep the card's visual identity (background, stroke, colors) instead of collapsing it into a plain list

why: Concrete, well-reasoned before/after critiques of student responsive-card designs.

title: Designing Forms in Figma - UI/UX Challenge
why: No caption file - judged from title only. Forms are a relevant UI topic; likely Figma-heavy like the other challenge videos.

title: UI/UX Form Design DO's and DON'Ts! Review

best.what: concrete form fixes: fill empty layout space intelligently, group related fields, keep checkbox/input styling consistent, link the terms-and-conditions text

why: The single strongest form-design video in the group - specific, correct, and directly reusable for any form the kids build (e.g. a Sheets-backed signup screen).

title: UI/UX Prototyping and Animation in Figma  (Challenge)
why: Entirely about Figma's own component-variant/prototype authoring system (smart animate, on-hover triggers) - doesn't map onto how kids would actually build CSS/JS animation with Gemini.

title: Who made the BEST UI Prototyping Animation?

best.what: "speedy, snappy" motion with spring/bounce easing praised over slow, gradual animation - a transferable feel lesson even outside Figma

why: The pacing/easing commentary (fast vs. slow, simultaneous vs. sequential) is a real game-feel/animation lesson, even though it's reviewing Figma prototypes.

title: Using Generative AI in UI/UX Design
why: Generating background art with Midjourney and compositing it in Photoshop/Illustrator - a different kind of "AI" than prompting Gemini to write code, and off our tool stack.

title: The World of Embellishments in UI/UX Design (Challenge)

best.what: same layout, three different accent-graphic treatments, each changing the mood/message of the page

why: The idea that visual accents set mood/theme is useful for character and game-feel work, but the execution is pen-tool/Midjourney/Photoshop compositing that won't transfer directly.

title: Who made the BEST UI/UX Layout from THIS Challenge?
why: No caption file - judged from title only. Review of the embellishments challenge; likely similar mixed value to P96IGCr93IA.

title: The UI/UX of Light / Dark Mode Design (Challenge)

best.what: the dark-mode rule of thumb: shift lightness on the same hue rather than jumping to pure black/white, and recheck contrast on every element

why: A genuinely useful, common feature request (dark mode) with a real design rule behind it, but taught through 14 minutes of Figma hex-value picking.

title: It's time to design your portfolio - CHALLENGE!
why: Designing a personal/agency design portfolio - explicitly a career/portfolio topic the brief excludes.

title: 6 UI/UX Design Refactors of Design Portfolios
why: Review of design-portfolio hero sections - same career/portfolio topic as FsYi-O9-ZVw, out of scope even though the critiques themselves are competent.

title: Designing CONSISTENT Sub Pages | UI/UX Challenge

best.what: the brief for a consistent sub-page: reuse the same nav, colors and type so a second page still feels like the same product

why: Consistency-across-screens and simple list-item design (label + value + action button) are directly useful for a multi-screen app, but heavily Figma-mechanical.

title: Who Designed the BEST Sub Page for this Layout?
why: No caption file - judged from title only. Review companion to YVdm3e1NBf4.

title: Designing Dashboards in Figma | UI/UX Challenge
why: No caption file - judged from title only. Dashboards are relevant to a Sheets-backed app; the companion review (uMQnKUIXUSI) is core-quality, so this challenge video is probably useful but Figma-heavy.

title: Dashboard UI/UX Design Reviews | Who did it best?

best.what: the single biggest dashboard fix: light background + white cards beats gray cards with drop shadows, plus a 12-13px minimum text-size rule and the WCAG contrast check

why: Directly relevant to any stats/panel screen the kids build; concrete, correct, and example-driven rather than tool mechanics.

title: Most UI/UX Designers will Fail this Challenge
why: Pure challenge announcement (pick one of 20 AI-generated concepts) - no teaching content.

title: FINAL UI/UX Review for the 30 Day Challenge

best.what: rapid concrete fixes across varied UIs: dashboard card spacing/alignment, avoiding gray for interactive elements, panel color contrast

why: Broad, quick, concrete before/after tips across many different UI types - a strong closer for the format.

title: Interactive UI/UX Crash Course
why: Confirmed word-for-word compilation of every other video in this group (all 30 days stitched into one 5h45m file) - a pure duplicate, not new material.
